purpose: Distinguish local adaptation error from limitations of the released Squidiff protocol
primary_metrics: iPSC transient peak excess and amplitude
checkpoint_policy: Evaluate fixed final checkpoint and EMA; never select a seed/checkpoint using the desired T peak
sampling_policy: Report fixed sigma=0.7 source setting and the prior validation-selected sigma separately

stages.question: Are equations, optimizer updates, sampler and checkpoint restore equivalent to public code?
Does removing BF16 or TF32 fix the failures?
Do conclusions persist over independent training seeds?
Do published preprocessing, full training groups or the HVG scope explain the difference?
Can the same network recover transient states when intermediate training cells are provided?
stages.scope: diagnostic; changes the information available and cannot count as endpoint-only success

test_use: Existing tests are now diagnostic development benchmarks; any new method improvement needs fresh final holdout evaluation
disk_policy: Keep raw data, source hashes, metrics, predictions, final weights and one complete latest optimizer state per active run; remove redundant checkpoints if free space falls below 20 GiB
